title: 35yo F - Palpitations (Unstable SVT)
background: Patient presents to the ER complaining of a sudden onset of a 'racing heart'. She now feels extremely dizzy and looks pale.

exam.finding: Tachycardic, weak thready pulse, no murmurs

investigations.name: 12-Lead ECG
investigations.report: Narrow complex tachycardia at 185 bpm. No visible P waves. Regular rhythm.

start.narrative: ECG confirms SVT. The patient is hypotensive (80/50) and symptomatic (dizzy, diaphoretic). This indicates an UNSTABLE tachycardia according to ACLS guidelines.

correct_cardioversion.narrative: Excellent! Synchronized cardioversion immediately converted the rhythm to Normal Sinus Rhythm. Blood pressure improved and the patient is no longer dizzy.

wrong_adenosine.narrative: Adenosine is for STABLE narrow-complex tachycardia. Delaying electrical therapy in an unstable patient causes further deterioration. The patient loses consciousness.

wrong_defib.narrative: FATAL ERROR! You delivered an unsynchronized shock (Defibrillation) during the relative refractory period (R-on-T phenomenon), sending the patient into Ventricular Fibrillation! Cardiac Arrest!

wrong_vagal.narrative: Vagal maneuvers take time and are ineffective for a hemodynamically UNSTABLE patient. The patient continues to deteriorate.
